identity_and_scope.principle: Religion, sovereignty and occupation memory can be culturally central without assigning belief, trauma or resistance history to every Bajoran.

misread_risks: Religious language does not prove personal orthodoxy.
Strong sovereignty language does not prove hostility to Federation personnel.
Occupation memory does not prove personal trauma or resistance service.

rules: Civil government and religious authority are separate systems.
Religious title does not automatically grant civil authority.
Resistance history, militia/service and government role require explicit character state.

privacy_and_intimacy.rule: Faith and trauma may be private; AI cannot infer either from species.

work_service_and_profession.rule: Species does not imply priesthood, militia/resistance service or government employment.

rules: Faith intensity and interpretation are individual/cultural state.
Religious institutions and civil institutions are represented separately.

law_duty_and_obligation.rule: Civil jurisdiction, religious expectation and personal belief must not be collapsed.

common_misreads: every Bajoran is anti-Cardassian in identical ways
cross_cultural_interaction.professional_response: Ask which history, faith, institution and individual experience actually apply.

notes: Pre-occupation, occupation and post-occupation/reconstruction contexts must not be mixed.
Campaign state after start may diverge from later canon outcomes.

ai_guardrails: Do not assign faith or orthodoxy by species.
Do not invent trauma or resistance service.
Do not let religious authority silently become civil authority.
Do not treat all Cardassian-related reactions as identical.
